subject: ela
intro: Eleventh graders demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics. American literary movements (Puritan, Transcendentalist, Realist, and others) each explored distinctive themes.

items.prompt:
Transcendentalist writers like Emerson and Thoreau emphasized the individual and nature.

What shared THEME did they explore?

steps: Both stressed self-reliance and a spiritual connection to nature.
So a shared theme is the value of individual conscience and nature.
solution.answer: The value of individual self-reliance and a spiritual bond with nature.

items.prompt: Why compare two works from the SAME PERIOD on a similar theme?

steps: Comparing them shows how the era's writers shared and varied ideas.
So it reveals how the period's writers treated a common theme differently.
solution.answer: To see how writers of the same era treated a common theme similarly and differently.

items.prompt: A literary MOVEMENT is a what?

steps: A movement is a group of writers sharing styles and ideas in a period.
So it is a shared literary style and set of ideas in a period.
solution.answer: A shared literary style and set of ideas among writers of a period.

items.prompt: A group of writers sharing ideas in a period is a literary ____.
Comparing two same-period works shows shared ____.
